original_test_intent: Exercise the intended CPU thermal-control path with the approved MODS module and load profile, demonstrating controlled temperature/frequency/power behavior, healthy cooling and error-free recovery within platform limits.
original_method: Obtain a signed/versioned MODS package and exact CPU thermal module/arguments; bind CPU sockets, cooling zones and sensors; preserve baseline telemetry/logs; drain workloads; perform a short approved preflight before the qualified duration; monitor per-socket/package temperatures, frequency/throttle reasons, power, fan/pump and ambient state from independent OS/BMC sources; use hard abort thresholds; preserve full tool/result/telemetry and prove post-load recovery without automatically rerunning.
manual_activity: A qualified thermal/platform operator validates cooling, supervises the maintenance window and owns the physical emergency stop and recovery path.
required_inputs: MODS package version/hash/signature/license, supported platform and module guide
Exact CPU thermal module, arguments, load level, warm-up, duration, repetitions and result semantics
CPU/socket/BIOS/microcode, heatsink/TIM/fan/pump/ambient configuration and calibrated sensor map
Temperature/power/frequency/throttle/error limits, sampling cadence, abort thresholds and cooldown/recovery criteria
safety_requirements: Do not execute while procedure and criteria remain TBD
Drain jobs/users and verify redundant cooling plus BMC/console recovery before load
Monitor independent OS and BMC sensors continuously with hard limits and an operator stop path
Abort once on cooling failure, threshold crossing, unexpected throttling, hardware error, hang or crash
Preserve evidence; do not automatically retry a thermal anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Validate package authenticity, exact recipe, target CPU/sensors, limits and recovery
Perform read-only baseline and, only after explicit approval, run the exact supplied MODS command while logging telemetry
Stop at approved abort conditions and collect cooldown/post-health evidence without verdict
Do not invent module/arguments, clear logs, override protections, restart a failed run or operate physical cooling/recovery
engineer_actions: Approve MODS package/platform support and exact thermal recipe
Approve cooling configuration, independent sensor oracle, acceptance/abort/cooldown criteria and recovery
Supervise risk controls and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `mods -h` only establishes binary availability; its malformed SSH form and `head` truncation neither identify nor execute CPU thermal coverage. The actual command must come from the vendor recipe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After package/recipe/telemetry checks and explicit confirmation, run the exact owner-approved MODS CPU thermal module once with full stdout/stderr/exit status and synchronized OS/BMC telemetry.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source supplies only 10/10-minute estimates; no load, duration or criteria are inferred from those estimates or from the neighboring DVFS case.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH PACKAGE-GATED CPU THERMAL STRESS AND CONTROL-LOOP VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run one approved MODS thermal profile under redundant telemetry and hard abort control, then verify cooldown, frequency restoration and error-free health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Fills no TBD value speculatively; instead defines the exact vendor, cooling, telemetry, limit, abort and recovery decisions required before execution.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: MODS help or generic CPU load cannot prove the intended vendor thermal module, control behavior or qualified acceptance criteria.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A tool/module mismatch or sensor-label error can overheat the wrong socket unnoticed; short source timing may be insufficient for thermal steady state unless engineering approves it.

project_override_considerations: The project must define whether success is merely no shutdown/error or also temperature plateau, sustained clock/power, absence/expected degree of throttling and fan response. Sensor tolerances and ambient inlet conditions belong in the oracle.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approval and MODS package/module/recipe identity
Preflight plus full timestamped MODS stdout/stderr/exit status and actual duration/load
Synchronized per-socket temperature/frequency/power/throttle and fan/pump/ambient telemetry
Preserved EDAC/MCE/kernel/SEL/BMC/boot evidence and abort markers
Cooldown/recovery-to-baseline record, anomalies and engineer verdict

review_improvement: Converts the TBD thermal case into a traceable decision set without inventing a dangerous command and requires independent telemetry plus one-shot abort/recovery discipline.
independent_technical_reasoning: The title establishes a thermal-control objective but no executable semantics. `mods -h` cannot validate load or safety, and copying the prior CPUDVFS recipe would conflate frequency-transition coverage with thermal saturation. A valid run needs an exact vendor module, per-socket sensor mapping and cooling oracle, with synchronized frequency/power/throttle behavior. Since load can produce irreversible damage or service loss, threshold breach terminates the attempt and is preserved rather than retried.
